A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B. Appendix reordering and figure renumbering can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original bandit simulations and language-model experiments on MATH, HARP, CodeContests, and TACO, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds GRPO/Dr. GRPO experiments in Appendix A.2 and Table 3.

M1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds GRPO/Dr. GRPO adaptations: removing the learned value baseline from the clipped PPO update and optionally normalizing the effective advantages by their standard deviation. The core leave-one-out and biased gradient estimators remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same bandit, mathematical reasoning, and code-generation coverage. The new GRPO experiments reuse CodeContests and TACO, including their existing evaluation splits.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds evaluated mean-objective GRPO and Dr. GRPO baselines against corresponding biased pass@k variants. The original policy-gradient and PPO comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: The added GRPO experiment evaluates Llama 3.1 8B Instruct after 8,000 training steps and reports pass@1/pass@10 averaged across checkpoints at 7,200–8,000 steps, spaced 200 steps apart. Existing experiments retain their settings.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds a check of whether the pass@k advantage persists with critic-free updates, both with and without standard-deviation normalization. Existing sample-count, model-size, HARP, and generalization analyses are retained despite appendix moves.

E5.justification: v2 introduces averaging performance over the final five checkpoints for Table 3, explicitly to avoid cherry-picking. This adds an estimation procedure, not five independent runs; no seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and all 16 existing plots retain their results. New Table 3 reports higher pass@10 but lower pass@1 for biased pass@k under both GRPO methods. For example, CodeContests test pass@10 is 16.44 versus 14.89 for Dr. GRPO and 15.45 versus 14.41 for GRPO.

T1.justification: The unbiasedness and biased-objective lemmas, their proofs, and Appendix B's majority-voting, leave-p-out, and softmax reasoning are retained. The GRPO addition specializes existing update formulas without adding a new theoretical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: optimizing inference-time objectives through reinforcement learning and demonstrating objective-dependent performance trade-offs. The new GRPO evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 7 removes its synthesis linking gains to mean-performance/sample-diversity trade-offs, relative model capability, and alignment between mean and inference-time objectives. Related experimental interpretations remain elsewhere, and the computational-cost and credit-assignment limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 documents the GRPO adaptations, reuse of existing hyperparameters, and the precise training/checkpoint-averaging recipe. Earlier preprocessing, PPO implementation, and experimental details are retained after relocation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shao et al. (2024) and Liu et al. (2025), connecting the approach to GRPO and Dr. GRPO through its effective-reward formulation. The existing related-work discussion otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 moves code-generation details from Appendix A.4 to A.2, shifts the subsequent appendix subsections, shortens Section 7, and adds an Impact Statement and conference/contact information. Most existing prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3 and boldface score highlighting in Tables 1–2. Appendix figures are relocated and renumbered, and Algorithm 1 moves, while the original plots retain their content and design. Running headers and spacing also change.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.2 and Table 3 modestly strengthen the paper by testing the objective trade-off under GRPO and Dr. GRPO with an explicit checkpoint-averaging procedure. This adds useful evidence without altering earlier results. Although Section 7 loses a useful interpretive synthesis and independent-run uncertainty remains unreported, the documented extension provides a limited net improvement.
